class_hint: Harness update breaks a poller assumption (silently)
instance: The third-party harnesses (codex CLI, hermes) update WEEKLY by design — they are deliberately NOT pinned (currency is wanted). The risk is not drift per se but a weekly update silently changing an interface the poller depends on (an `codex exec` flag renamed/removed, the `hermes chat` invocation changing) with no signal — the loop stalls or misbehaves quietly.
check: Do NOT pin the harnesses (founder directive: keep them current). Instead make the integration RESILIENT: (1) a tiny harness-contract smoke test exercising the exact `codex exec`/`hermes chat` invocation the poller uses, run on a schedule + after any detected version change; (2) fail-LOUD on interface breakage (non-zero exit / changed flags surface an alert, never a silent exit-0 — see FM-18); (3) re-probe capabilities/version rather than assuming (ASK-don't-infer); (4) record the observed harness version each cycle so a break correlates to an update.

check: Every periodic-maintenance method (reaper/GC/sweeper) must have a call site in the daemon loop AND a test that asserts the loop invokes it (or that its effect occurs end-to-end). Grep: each exported `Reap*`/`GC*`/`Sweep*` has a non-test caller. Distrust comments that claim a routine "also runs" — verify the call.

instance: A dispatched client passed its own unit tests but violated the SERVER wire contract, because neither the issue spec nor the generated tests pinned the contract: it sent `priority` as a string when `enqueueReq.priority` is an int (→ 400) and omitted the required `expected_delivery:comment_only` signal (→ artifact-gate fail-loud). Green tests gave false confidence; the bug only surfaced against the live API (claude-codex fleet-consult #180, fixed #181/#182).
check: When briefing a client/wrapper that speaks an existing wire API, pin the contract in the spec (exact field names, JSON types, required signal fields) AND require at least one acceptance test that runs against the real endpoint (or a contract fixture derived from the server struct), not only mocked-curl unit tests. Coordinator runs a live smoke-test before merge.

Key-length 65 vs the clean 64 of working tokens was the tell.
check: Generate token material without a trailing newline (`openssl rand -hex 32 \

instance: `kubectl patch`/`kubectl replace` on a k8s Secret managed by ExternalSecrets Operator (ESO) silently succeeds (rc=0, resourceVersion bumps) but ESO reconciles the change back within seconds — observed on `fleet-dispatch-tokens` in `ai-fleet`. Additionally, ATTACH_TOKENS was injected as an env var (not a volume mount), so a pod restart is required after every update; restarting before ESO finishes writing the Secret loads the old value into the new pods (race condition independently identified by Codex and Hermes during fleet-plan dry run, 2026-06-18).
check: Before patching any k8s Secret, check for a matching ExternalSecret (`kubectl get externalsecret <name> -n <ns>`). If one exists, the ONLY write path is through the external store (Infisical/Vault). Mandatory sequence: (1) update source-of-truth store via MCP/API, (2) annotate ExternalSecret with `force-sync=$(date +%s)` to trigger immediate reconcile, (3) POLL Secret resourceVersion until it changes — never proceed until confirmed, (4) restart the deployment ONLY after the Secret reflects the new value, (5) run a smoke test that proves the running application received the new config. Also applies to token authorization splits: verify BOTH `produces` (enqueue) and `consumes` (claim) fields contain required capabilities — missing either yields different HTTP errors (403 vs `{"empty":true}`).

instance: A terminal SUCCESS signal was treated as proof the work succeeded. A fleet-dispatch `impl-grok` review task was enqueued, the Grok consumer claimed the lease (`lease_holder: grok`) and reported `state: done` — and that was announced as "fully wired, end-to-end confirmed." But the job produced nothing usable: the consumer never injected the referenced GitHub issue body (Grok's own reasoning said "I need to find what article they're referring to"), the stored result was truncated to exactly **1024 bytes** of opening reasoning, and no comment was mirrored to the issue. `done` described the queue lifecycle, not the deliverable (2026-06-18).
check: Never accept a terminal/OK status (`done`, rc=0, HTTP 200, lease-claimed, "tests pass") as evidence the work succeeded — verify the DELIVERABLE. For any dispatch/queue/agent round-trip assert: (1) the input/`ref` payload actually reached the worker; (2) `result_bytes` is plausible and non-truncated (a round cap like 1024 is a tell), and the content actually answers the task; (3) any promised side-channel (issue comment, branch push, output file) actually landed. A status field is a CLAIM the system makes about its own lifecycle (an observation); the artifact is the evidence. This is the observation-vs-conclusion error applied to a status field: "item is `done`" is the observation, "the work succeeded" is the unverified conclusion.

class_hint: Install / Config Layout — env-var override masks `.env`
instance: `host-update.sh` set `HOSTNAME="$(hostname -f)"` as an inline env-var assignment before `docker compose up -d`; Docker Compose prefers a shell env-var over the project `.env` file, so the machine's short hostname (`gx10-b6b9`) always overrode the `.env`'s correct fleet FQDN (`oblivion.petersimmons.com`). Controller matched the reported hostname against GPUHost CRDs, found nothing, returned HTTP 401 → watcher heartbeat never updated → controller stopped advertising the host → Olla excluded it → model invisible (2026-06-18, aifleet#96).
check: In any `compose up -d` wrapper script: prefer `.env` over machine hostname by reading `.env` explicitly (`sed -n 's/^HOSTNAME=//p' .env`), falling back to `hostname -f` only when absent. Never use `VAR="$(dynamic-cmd)"` as an inline assignment before `docker compose` when `.env` holds the authoritative value for that variable.

class_hint: Fail-Loud — NFS transient mount failure marks container degraded
instance: Docker volume backed by NFS (`truenas:/mnt/zp1/ai-models`) occasionally returns "connection refused" at `docker compose up` time. The watcher's `applyPolicy()` catches the pull/start failure and enters `pull_failed_backoff` (300s). The host does not self-heal until the watcher is restarted or the backoff window expires. The NFS mount itself is fine after a few seconds — the transient is at `docker volume` mount time. Observed on oblivion; resolved on its own once the NFS server's ARP cache settled (2026-06-18).
check: NFS-backed Docker volumes: if a model container enters `pull_failed_backoff` immediately after a host restart or watcher restart, check `docker volume inspect ai-fleet-models` and `docker run --rm -v ai-fleet-models:/mnt busybox ls /mnt` before concluding the model or image is broken. Transient NFS refusals are self-clearing; re-run `host-update.sh` or `docker compose restart watcher` to clear the backoff. Long-term fix: watcher should distinguish "NFS mount failed" from "image pull failed" and use a shorter retry interval for the former.

instance: Used the **diagnostics-only `ssh` path for agent coordination** (running Grok/Codex/Hermes reviews, prompt-TDD, and collab via `ssh … docker exec … <agent> --single/-q`) instead of the sanctioned **ssh-free fleet-dispatch** path (`scripts/fleet-consult.sh`, `scripts/fleet-enqueue.sh`). The operating directive is explicit: *"ssh is DIAGNOSTICS ONLY; never for coordination."* Worse than a style violation: ssh-bypassing the queue **masks whether the real capability works** — I kept getting answers via ssh, which hid that the fleet `impl-grok` path was broken and turned the fix (PR #248) into theater, because I never exercised the thing I was fixing (2026-06-19).
check: All agent coordination — reviews, prompt-TDD, collab, consults — goes through fleet-dispatch **ssh-free**: `fleet-consult.sh` (Hermes Q&A), `fleet-enqueue.sh` (impl/review/impl-grok). Reserve `ssh` strictly for diagnostics (inspecting a process, logs, env). If a worker's fleet path is broken, that worker is **BLOCKED** until the path is fixed AND deployed — never substitute the ssh backdoor to fake the capability or to manufacture progress. Corollary to FM-87: don't just avoid trusting a fake status; don't manufacture a real-looking result through a channel that proves nothing about the system you're supposed to be building.

instance: After rotating `ATTACH_TOKENS`, the fleet-dispatch pod was restarted but only one consumer (Hermes or Codex) was cycled. The un-cycled consumer continued authenticating with the old token — receiving 401 on every claim attempt — stalling work silently for hours until the consumer was manually restarted. Root cause: Codex and Hermes each hold an independent copy of their bearer credential (Codex: `~/.config/fleet-dispatch/token` on the codex node; Hermes: an env-var/Secret mount). Neither is hot-reloaded; both must be cycled in the same rotation window.

Critical lockstep gate: after rotating `ATTACH_TOKENS` in Infisical → force-syncing ESO → confirming Secret `resourceVersion` bumped → restarting fleet-dispatch, BOTH consumers must be cycled before the old token window closes. Deterministic check: after rotation, run `scripts/fleet-canary.sh` and assert each consumer returns a successful terminal `done` within N seconds. A 401 from any consumer after rotation means the lockstep step was skipped.

Root cause: sibling consumers share a contract but not a code path; a patch to one does not propagate to the other. (2026-06-19, fleet-dispatch)

instance: Attach service shows `active`/polling, zero auth errors, but every claimed item fails on a local precondition (dirty working tree / missing branch) — the service passes all liveness and status checks while doing zero real work. Because liveness probes only verify the process, not the work-execution path, the failure is invisible until a round-trip canary times out. (2026-06-19, codex-attach.service)
check: A process/liveness check is NOT a work-execution check. Complement all consumer liveness probes with a scheduled real round-trip canary that enqueues a minimal item and asserts a terminal `done` within a bounded window. A consumer that claims but never completes is indistinguishable from a healthy consumer unless the deliverable is verified. Cross-ref FM-87 (terminal status ≠ deliverable success).

instance: Fleet-dispatch capability strings are free-form text gated only by token Produces/Consumes lists. Detection requires polling the item status manually. (2026-06-19)

Detection check: `enqueue → poll → assert state != queued after N seconds`.

class_hint: Install / Config Layout — ATTACH_TOKENS atomic-blob hazard
instance: `ATTACH_TOKENS` is a single JSON object keyed by live bearer hex strings. Any edit (add/remove/rotate a token) requires a full read-merge-write cycle. A JSON syntax error during that cycle (malformed merge, trailing comma, copy-paste mistake) corrupts the entire map and returns 401 to ALL consumers simultaneously — the fleet closes hard with no partial fallback. One bad token rotation can silently kill the entire dispatch bus. (2026-06-19, fleet-dispatch)
check: Treat `ATTACH_TOKENS` as crown-jewel config: (1) always read the current value, apply a structured merge tool (e.g. `jq` merge), and JSON-validate (`jq . >/dev/null`) before writing; (2) retain the previous value in a rollback variable for the duration of the rotation window; (3) after write, verify the new token works on a canary request before the old token is invalidated; (4) enforce supervised edits only — no raw `kubectl edit`. Cross-ref FM-86 (ESO-managed secret write path).

class_hint: Deploy / Verify Discipline — acting on unverified diagnosis (diagnosis drift)

In both cases, a fix was built and deployed before the diagnosis was confirmed with a live probe. Cross-ref FM-70 (trust calibration: observation vs. conclusion). (2026-06-19)

class_hint: Agent Coordination — Batch-dispatch of semi-related tasks produces N conflicting PRs
instance: Coordinator dispatches N individually-queued Codex issues for a batch of tasks in the same repo without grouping by file-area ownership. Codex picks them all up in parallel, opens N draft PRs simultaneously, and they conflict each other on shared files (e.g., docker-compose.yml, go flags files, docs). Root cause: parallel-safe check only catches exact file-path overlap in plan files, not "same file-area" overlap. A batch of OOBE fixes touching cmd/, deploy/, docs/ in one repo is effectively one logical unit dispatched as N separate units. Cost: N round-trips to Codex for rebases; wasted CI cycles; merge churn. Fix: (1) GROUP by file-area — bundle tasks that span the same repo+file-area into 1–3 issues by area (cmd/ fixes → one issue, deploy/ fixes → one issue, docs fixes → one issue); (2) if keeping separate issues, enforce strict sequence — remove parallel-safe from all but the first; each must merge before the next is dispatched; (3) never mark issues parallel-safe within the same repo batch unless file sets are truly disjoint (different packages, different service boundaries). Introduced: 2026-06-22 — factvault OOBE batch (issues #210–#217, 8 issues → 8 simultaneous PRs → 5 conflicts on first merge pass).
check: Judgment

class_hint: Agent Coordination / Dispatch — fleet-enqueue with short repo name → malformed ref → silent dead-letter
instance: Enqueuing a fleet-dispatch item with bare repo name (e.g., `--repo factvault`) instead of full slug (`--repo petersimmons1972/factvault`). The enqueue command SUCCEEDS and returns an enqueue ID, giving false confidence. The codex-attach consumer requires refs in `[HOST/]OWNER/REPO` format; a bare name produces a malformed ref. Consumer cannot resolve it, item never claims, queue reaper dead-letters it within seconds. GitHub issue label stays `agent/codex/queued` (cosmetic), masking the failure. Compounding: discovered alongside a dead consumer (codex-agent container down ~10h); consumer downtime hid the slug bug because items dead-lettered for "no consumer" reasons instead of malformed ref. When consumer restarted, items STILL failed with "expected [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format, got factvault". Cost: hours of apparent "queued but idle" state; two false-start re-enqueue rounds. Introduced: 2026-06-23 — factvault #210/#211/#213/#216/#217 re-enqueue after OOBE batch rebases.
check: (1) ALWAYS use full `OWNER/REPO` slug to fleet-enqueue.sh (`petersimmons1972/factvault`), never bare repo name. (2) Enhance fleet-enqueue.sh to validate --repo arg matches `^[^/]+/[^/]+$` (or `[HOST/]OWNER/REPO`) and reject bare names at enqueue time (file enhancement on fleet-dispatch). (3) When items show `queued` on GitHub label but never claim, check actual queue item state via fleet-dispatch /items API — the label lies; the queue state is truth.

class_hint: Observability / Agent Coordination — Silent consumer death, no liveness/staleness alerting on dispatch pipeline
instance: The codex-attach consumer (Docker container codex-agent) died and stayed dead ~10 hours. Nothing alerted. The queue kept accepting enqueues; ~50 items dead-lettered silently, and GitHub issue labels stayed cosmetically `agent/codex/queued`. Discovered only by manual inspection after PRs sat idle. Root cause: no automated detection for "consumer alive but not consuming" or "consumer dead." Three missing detection layers: (1) Consumer liveness — no per-capability last-claim heartbeat + staleness alert; (2) Queue health — no alert on items queued > N min unclaimed, no dead-letter-rate alert (50 dead-letters accumulated with zero notification); (3) End-to-end canary — no scheduled synthetic item proving the pipeline completes work. Compounding: GitHub labels are cosmetic and lie (stay `queued`); the fleet-dispatch /items API is the only truth source for actual queue state. Cost: ~10h pipeline outage undetected; multiple false-start re-enqueues; manual diagnosis. Observed: 2026-06-23 — codex-agent container dead during factvault OOBE rebase cycle, items dead-lettered in silence.
check: (1) Per-capability liveness: alert when a capability has queued items but no consumer claim/heartbeat in 15 min. (2) Queue-health alerts: item-age threshold + dead-letter-rate spike alert. (3) Scheduled end-to-end canary (enqueue trivial no-op every ~10 min; alert if not completed within SLA) — catches ALL pipeline failure causes regardless of root cause. (4) Container-level: Docker healthcheck that probes the attach-loop liveness (not just process-exists) + autoheal sidecar for self-recovery; keep canary alerting so silent auto-restarts don't mask deeper faults. Tracked: fleet-dispatch#65 (canary + LAST_SUCCESS staleness) covers layers 1+3; fleet-dispatch#67 (structured harness logging) feeds the alerting. Prioritize #65 to p1 after this incident.

class_hint: Fail-Loud / Fleet-Dispatch — Fleet consumer silently not claiming: wrong-token default + gate-reset-on-deploy, no alerting
instance: Queued items for capability `impl-grok` sat indefinitely with `retries=0`, `lease_holder:""`. Consumer container healthy (uptime + healthcheck pass), fleet-dispatch server healthy, no error surfaced anywhere. Compound root causes: (1) `deploy-grok-machine.sh:~51` defaults `FLEET_TOKEN_FILE` to `token-impl` (Codex token) instead of `token-impl-grok`; server returns `{empty:true}` on every `/claim` because that token's `consumes` set lacks the target capability — silently; (2) `deploy-grok-machine.sh:~127` always writes `GROK_ATTACH_ENABLED=0`, disabling claiming on every redeploy regardless of prior state; (3) no alert fires on "items queued with no lease for N minutes" or "consumer token `consumes` does not include its target capability." Burned a multi-step diagnostic cycle (poll → k8s health → host docker → token-sha comparison) before isolating the cause. (Bug: petersimmons1972/claude-codex#316)
check: (a) Deploy default must use the capability-specific token (`token-impl-grok`), not the generic `token-impl`; validate at startup. (b) Persist gate state across redeploys, or make ENABLED the default post-cutover. (c) Consumer must log LOUDLY at startup when its token's `consumes` does not include the capability it was deployed to serve. (d) Alert on queue items with `lease_holder:""` older than N minutes and on a consumer whose token `consumes` is empty for its intended capability. Detection: `docker logs <consumer> --tail=25` → "standing by (disabled mode)" or empty-claim loops; compare token sha256 vs intended capability token; `GET /item/<id>` for persistent empty `lease_holder`.

class_hint: Fail-Loud / Infra / Config-Drift — Running container/config drifts from manifest: hand-edits and deploy resets diverge live state from source-of-truth, neither reconciles
instance: The live running container's effective config differs from what the declared manifest / deploy script / IaC source-of-truth would produce. Hand-fixes to the running host (sed-editing a live `.env`, `kubectl patch` on a secret) appear applied but are silently reverted on the next deploy or by ESO reconciliation; conversely, deploy scripts overwrite intended runtime state (e.g. resetting an enable gate to 0) on every run. "What's running" ≠ "what's declared," and nothing flags the gap. Root causes: (1) Deploy script writes authoritative values that overwrite operationally-critical runtime state on every redeploy (`deploy-grok-machine.sh:~127` forces `GROK_ATTACH_ENABLED=0`); (2) Operators hand-patch live state to work around it (sed on `.env`), creating drift the next deploy silently reverts; (3) ESO-managed k8s secrets (`fleet-dispatch-tokens`) have their source of truth in Infisical; direct `kubectl patch` looks applied but is reverted on next sync; (4) No drift detection comparing running effective config to the declared manifest / IaC source. Each layer (enable gate, consumer token, server-side `consumes` registration) gets patched at the LIVE container instead of at the source of truth, so it re-breaks on the next reconcile/deploy. Cost: this session — a hand-edited gate and a proposed k8s-secret patch would each have been reverted; compounded the FM-119 diagnostic chase. Related: FM-119, petersimmons1972/claude-codex#316.
check: After ANY deploy or ESO sync, diff the running container's effective env/config against (a) the deploy script's output and (b) the IaC source; re-verify runtime invariants (gate on, token identity, consumes set). Make every config change at the source of truth only — Infisical `ATTACH_TOKENS` for tokens/consumes (then force-sync + rollout-restart), the deploy script defaults / committed `.env` template for runtime flags — never hand-edit live state. Deploy scripts must PRESERVE operationally-critical state (don't hard-reset an enable gate). Add a reconcile/drift check (running vs declared) to the consumer healthcheck so divergence is loud, not silent.

class_hint: Deploy / Verify Discipline — live-deploy drift / running-ahead-of-manifest (extends FM-120)
instance: A running container or host-installed artifact is ahead of its source-of-truth: a `cp`/hand-edit applied to a live container without the identical change committed to source + image; a deployment rolled to an image tag the repo manifest does not pin; a `kubectl apply` of a change not yet on `main`. On the next rebuild, restart, or GitOps reconcile the running state silently regresses — symptom appears hours or days later with no clear cause. Observed: fleet-dispatch overnight runs #76/#78 (in-container `git pull`+`cp` of codex-poll NFF+lint patches); any `kubectl set image` outside a PR cycle.
check: (a) Manifest-first: before or simultaneously with any deploy, commit the change to source AND update the manifest/image so rebuild reproduces running state exactly. (b) After any deploy, run `~/bin/check-manifest-drift.sh` and assert PASS before closing the task. (c) Drift = wake-the-founder-class incident. Detection: automated CronJob `manifest-drift-check` in `ai-fleet` namespace (`aifleet/controller/deploy/manifest-drift-cronjob.yaml`, founder-gated apply). Manual check: `~/bin/check-manifest-drift.sh`.

class_hint: Infra / vLLM — Stale flag in docs causes crash-loop on cutover: `--disable-frontend-multiprocessing` removed in vLLM V1
instance: During Qwen2.5-72B production cutover on oblivion (2026-06-25), the new GPUHost CRD included `--disable-frontend-multiprocessing` based on `spark/docs/vllm-builds.md` which documented it as "required for stable GB10 operation." vLLM v0.20.0 (V1 engine) does not recognize this flag — `unrecognized arguments: --disable-frontend-multiprocessing`. The container crash-looped for ~3 min while the watcher kept recreating it. Root cause: the flag was valid in earlier vLLM versions where the frontend/backend were separate processes, but vLLM V1 merged the architecture. The running Nemotron config had never included this flag and worked fine — the docs introduced a stale claim that the plan incorporated without verifying against the existing working config.
check: (1) Before adding any vLLM flag from docs/notes to a new model config, verify the flag exists in the target version: `docker run --rm --entrypoint '' <image> python3 -c "import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)"` then compare against existing working configs for that image version. (2) When updating an existing model config, diff the proposed flags against the working config rather than starting from documentation. (3) `vllm-builds.md` entries for specific flags should include the vLLM version range they apply to. Detection: `docker logs <container> --tail=5` immediately after watcher starts the new container — `unrecognized arguments` exits within seconds. Fix: remove the flag from the CRD and reapply; watcher reconverges on next 60s poll cycle.

class_hint: Install / Config Layout — Missing referenced script breaks BUG ACCOUNTABILITY protocol
instance: `~/bin/add-failure-mode.sh` is referenced in CLAUDE.md BUG ACCOUNTABILITY step 3(c) but the file does not exist. The protocol silently degrades to manual edits of failure-modes-standard.md, which are then skipped. (GitHub #308)
check: Every script referenced in CLAUDE.md, skills, or runbooks MUST exist at the stated path; verify with `ls -la` in the install check. (FM-123)

class_hint: Verify claimed fixes exist in the merged tree, not just in the PR description
instance: A merged PR (factvault #231) listed C-conformance fixes (feeds.yaml tenant match #211, worker rss --tenant #217) in its body that were never actually committed; a later close-sweep trusted the changelog and wrongly closed the issues. Detection: re-verify claimed fixes against the merged tree, not the PR description. Prevention: build-proof against code, never the changelog; verify-before-close.
check: Verify claimed fixes exist in the merged tree, not just in the PR description

class_hint: Stay on OAuth; confirmed fix: drop `--ephemeral` from relay/poller; never co-run Grok relay with its live daemon; do not exercise OAuth CLIs for diagnostics
instance: CONFIRMED (1): `codex exec --ephemeral` reads the rotated OAuth refresh token but never persists it back to auth.json (mtime frozen at last login while atime advances) → next call returns `refresh_token_invalidated`. Observer-effect confirmed: exercising any OAuth-backed CLI (`codex exec`, `grok --single`) or restarting the consumer container rotates/rewrites the shared auth.json and can destabilize other sessions. CONFIRMED (2): `docker exec grok-agent grok --single` co-runs a second grok in the same container as the live daemon, racing on one auth.json; no-TTY loser hangs indefinitely on device-code flow. UNCONFIRMED (demoted): rolling single-use token mutual revocation across leviathan/host/container stores — NOT verified; ChatGPT OAuth normally supports concurrent device sessions. Detection: `refresh_token_invalidated` / device-code prompt on a relay call; auth.json mtime frozen while atime advances. Resolution: STAY ON OAUTH. Drop `--ephemeral` from relay + poller. Never co-run the Grok relay while its daemon is live. Do not exercise OAuth CLIs for diagnostics. API-key cutover plan DROPPED. (fleet-dispatch, grok-agent, codex-attach, 2026-06-26)
check: Stay on OAuth; drop `--ephemeral`; never co-run Grok relay with live daemon; do not exercise OAuth CLIs for diagnostics

class_hint: Identity vs. Routing / Fail-Loud — duplicate consumer identity
instance: Two processes shared one token: a stale systemd `codex-attach.service` had been 401ing since 2026-06-25 alongside the container consumer. Its retry loop never exited, so `Restart=on-failure` never fired and systemd remained `active`; the unit also had no `WatchdogSec` or `OnFailure`. Observed in the 2026-07-03 audit ([claude-codex#362](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/claude-codex/issues/362)).
check: **Automated detection/alerting: none; manual signal: repeated 401 logs plus service/process inspection. Current mitigation: none.** Proposed: bind each distinct scoped credential to a stable consumer ID, reject a second concurrent session for that ID server-side, exit after a configured consecutive-401 threshold, and add systemd watchdog/failure notification.

class_hint: Delivery Durability / Fail-Loud — completed report discarded during Postgres outage
instance: A transient Postgres failure at report time can discard an otherwise completed LLM run: the Hermes consumer makes one `/report` attempt ([fleet-dispatch#133](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/fleet-dispatch/issues/133)), while Codex retries for only about 15 seconds. Structurally certain in the 2026-07-03 audit ([claude-codex#362](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/claude-codex/issues/362)).
check: **Durable lost-output/ack detection: none; a report-request failure may remain only in consumer logs. Current mitigation: partial only (Codex's approximately 15-second retry; none for Hermes).** Proposed: durably spool completed reports with restrictive permissions, bounded retention, and no secret-bearing logs; retry idempotently until acknowledged; alert and reconcile completed runs lacking an acknowledgement.

class_hint: Agent Coordination / Canary Integrity — no-consumer accumulation
instance: Canary items can enqueue indefinitely when no consumer claims their capability, so the canary certifies nothing while the queue grows ([fleet-dispatch#140](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/fleet-dispatch/issues/140)); identified in the 2026-07-03 audit ([claude-codex#362](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/claude-codex/issues/362)).
check: **Automated detection/alerting: none; manual signal: queued age and empty `lease_holder`. Current mitigation: none.** Proposed: fail enqueue when no authenticated, capability-authorized, fresh consumer registration exists; otherwise retain an auditable failed-canary result at the claim deadline and alert its owner.

class_hint: Fail-Loud / Observability — startup credential missing silent crash-loop
instance: In the opencode incident, an attach consumer crash-looped at startup because a required credential was missing. `ai-fleet-watcher` monitored model containers only, not attach consumers, so the failure was silent. The 2026-07-03 audit record ([claude-codex#362](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/claude-codex/issues/362)) is the sole incident reference supplied.
check: **Automated detection/alerting for attach consumers: none; manual signal: service/process restart inspection. Current mitigation: none.** Proposed: fail startup credential preflight loudly; alert the service owner on any preflight failure or crash loop and when the end-to-end attach canary exceeds its configured freshness interval.

class_hint: Deliverable Integrity / Semantic Validation — well-formed garbage accepted as `done`
instance: A `comment_only` report can be syntactically valid yet semantically empty and still reach `done`, because that lane has neither an artifact gate nor a semantic deliverable check; structurally certain at the `/report` acceptance boundary in the 2026-07-03 audit ([claude-codex#362](https://github.com/petersimmons1972/claude-codex/issues/362)).
check: **Automated semantic detection: none; manual signal: review the persisted `done` report. Current mitigation: none.** Proposed: reject terminal `done` unless the comment is non-empty, non-placeholder, and task-relevant; retain an explicit failed-validation state and cover the acceptance boundary with adversarial fixtures.

The vendor target docs/failure-modes.md collided with codex's own tracked docs/failure-modes.md -- an L0 SOURCE corpus -- and overwrote it. Recovery was possible only because git happened to be underneath (2026-08-01)

instance: The sync tool produced no undo. Recovery was improvised by hand from git state; had it written outside a repo or committed, undo would have been archaeology (2026-08-01)
check: An action must carry its own undo: emit an undo journal (every target path + prior state: absent/untracked/tracked+hash) BEFORE writing, and expose --undo. Reversibility inherited from the substrate is luck, not design.

instance: hindsight 2026-08-01: ARC scalesets are per-repo (10 exist, each with its own githubConfigUrl); the new repo had none, so every 'runs-on: homelab-arc' run queued indefinitely (~8h, 10+ runs, zero executions). PR #1 wired the CI and PASSED review; the only SUCCESS on all 5 PRs was GitGuardian. mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE was the sole signal.

source_anchor: Case Studies section, Case Study 1 -- Embedder Identity vs. Role Leak
instance: aifleet's per-role olla routing commit encoded GPU role into the --alias (bge-m3-live, bge-m3-reembed); engram-go read that alias as the persisted project_meta.embedder_name identity, so every memory_store returned embedder_mismatch and was blocked even though both endpoints served identical bge-m3 weights and no re-embed was actually needed. A secondary hazard: collapsing the names without a URL-based selector first would have sent a 259 GB bulk re-embed to the fanless MI-50.
check: Grep --alias values for role words before merging a routing commit; confirm the advertised alias equals the value persisted as the downstream identity; before collapsing names, confirm bulk-workload routing uses a selector other than the name being changed.

source_anchor: Case Studies section, Case Study 2 -- Poller Install-Layout / Repo Relocation
instance: The codex poller service had three compounding install-layout bugs: ExecStart referenced codex-poll.sh but the installer produced a binary named codex-poll (203/EXEC on every start); codex-liveness-check was referenced but never vendored, silently exit-127ing every 15 minutes for weeks with the wrapper masking it as success; and the poller infra lived in the wrong repo (codex tools repo) with a 128-line stub deployed in place of the real 2798-line poller.
check: Render ExecStart with real specifiers and diff against the post-install file listing; grep all unit targets and confirm source + install line exist in-repo; run git remote -v before editing to confirm the owning repo.

source_anchor: Case Studies section, standalone bullet (engram-go#1107), no FM-ID assigned in source
instance: An external-dependency HTTP call with no per-request read deadline wedged all workers indefinitely when an upstream gateway stalled a connection (zero bytes, ESTAB held for hours); the backends themselves were healthy -- the bug was the missing client timeout (engram-go#1107).
check: Every HTTP client against an external dependency must set http.Client{Timeout} or a per-call context.WithTimeout plus a bounded retry.

source_anchor: Bug Class D (Fail-Loud), inline bullet citing '(FM-112)' -- conflicts with the catalog table's actual FM-112 (factvault --addr flag); see notes
instance: An eval/measurement harness scored its own artifacts instead of the system under test: a probe that selected from sanitized gold-only inputs, applied a strawman filter, or over/under-extracted produced a headline number (e.g. a '4.7% floor') that looked like signal but actually measured the harness, with no per-stage instrumentation to reveal that the dominant failure was in the harness, not the SUT.
check: Instrument per-stage failure classes (extraction vs object-linking vs arithmetic vs gold-parse); add an upper-bound arm (e.g. no-object-filter) isolating the layer under test; run drop/perturbation sensitivity; red-team the harness itself.
